title: The Governing Question: The Structural Spine
use_cases: Use when you need to establish the core conflict within the first ten pages of a screenplay.
Implement when structuring scenes so each one advances toward resolving the governing dramatic question.
Configure when you want to avoid scene accumulation and ensure narrative momentum.
Use when analyzing why scenes fail to converge early in a script.
Apply when revising a screenplay to strengthen the central irreversible action.
content:
Every screenplay that holds is built around a governing dramatic question.

Not a theme.

Not a message.

A question that can only be answered through irreversible action.

Examples:

Will the protagonist sacrifice X to achieve Y

Can this relationship survive Z

Will the lie be exposed before it destroys everything

By page ten, the reader does not need the answer. They need to know what they are watching for.

Without a governing question, scenes accumulate instead of converge.

For how early structural instability destroys momentum, read Why Most Scripts Fail Before Page Ten.
